Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time to run through the demo today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we can get to a short POC fast: 

What we covered
- Integration focus: SDK bootstrap, auth pattern (short-lived keys + KMS), routing policies for latency vs cost, and structured outputs for downstream systems.
- Function fleet idea: model endpoints + tool adapters that can be invoked in parallel (search/embedding/rerank / external API calls) with a coordinator for error handling and fallbacks.
- Embeddings & reranker flow: client-side vectorization vs server-side batching tradeoffs; recommended starting with server-side embedding to centralize cache.

Key asks from Finexus
1) Confirm the primary POC scope (search augmentation + a single payment-exception tool call).
2) Provide sample dataset (5–10 example prompts + expected structured fields).
3) Agree on POC success criteria (latency < 400ms median, reranker top-3 precision > 75%).

Thanks Aditya — tagging in a few technical clarifications and an SDK checklist so Finexus has concrete items for their engineers.

Technical notes (high-level)
- SDK & bootstrap: we provide client SDKs (py/node) that handle KV cache pins, streaming, and function/tool call orchestration. Quickstart uses an API key with short TTL (15m) exchanged via your backend from an OIDC provider.
- Auth diagram (attached): our recommended pattern is: Finexus auth server issues short-lived JWT -> Redwood token exchange -> per-request ephemeral key. This avoids long-lived keys in the client.
- Routing: for production, create two policies — latency-first (route to smaller context models on high-cost hardware) and cost-first (batching on quantized variants). We can expose as named routes in the SDK (e.g., route: "latency-v1").
- Structured output: we recommend JSON schema + a lightweight validator in the SDK. If the tool call returns external API payloads, we wrap them in a canonical envelope {source, tool_id, status, payload}.

Function/fleet patterns & error handling
- Parallel invocation pattern: fire parallel calls to (1) embeddings lookup, (2) domain search API, (3) payment-exception tool. Use an async gather with per-call timeouts (recommended 250ms for non-critical ops, 350ms for reranker).
- Coordinator fallback rules: if reranker times out, fall back to embedding-only similarity + conservative confidence threshold. If payment-exception tool fails, return safe default with explicit human-review flag.
- Idempotency & retries: all tool adapters must be idempotent (tokenize calls where applicable) and use exponential backoff with jitter; mark retries in trace metadata.

POC checklist for engineers (quick items)
1) Install SDK (pip/ npm) and run the sample that hits the sandbox endpoints.
2) Exchange JWT and confirm token TTL behavior.
3) Wire up the embedding endpoint and verify vector dims.
4) Implement the function adapter for payment-exception call (we provide a template).
5) Run the included end-to-end demo locally and capture latency traces (we recommend the "p99-trace" mode).

I'll prepare the SDK quickstart repo and a minimal function adapter template by tomorrow morning. If Finexus engineering has infra constraints (no outbound traffic, strict egress), call that out so we can prepare an on-prem connector.

Adding a short architecture note from infra/ops perspective — pulled from patterns that scaled for similar customers.

Architecture suggestion (POC -> Prod):
- POC: use hosted Redwood sandbox models + a single dedicated function adapter in Finexus VPC via Private deployment connector. Keep data flow simple: request -> Redwood route -> model + adapters -> response.
- Prod: introduce a function-fleet controller that runs in your VPC and performs local tool calls (DB lookups, payments systems) while Redwood handles model inference. This minimizes egress and reduces latency for critical calls.

Parallel tools strategy:
- Tier tools by determinism: deterministic (DB lookup, auth check) vs heuristic (LLM-based reranker). Execute deterministic calls first and allow earlier short-circuiting when possible.
- Merge strategy: when results from search + embedding + reranker arrive, compute a weighted score where reranker has multiplicative boost only if confidence > 0.6. This reduces noisy reranker effects.

Observability & SLOs:
- Require traces for each tool call with parent/child spans. Surface a per-request timeline in the console for the POC.
- SLOs: median latency target 200–300ms per request in latency-first route; p95 < 800ms. We'll agree on final numbers for the SOW.

Security note:
- If Finexus needs a SOC2 evidence bundle, our compliance team can deliver a trimmed package for POC. For production, we'll need a short onboarding with your security team to confirm logging/retention choices.

I'll join the Friday tech sync if scheduled.
